result.title: Rep2Skill: Representation-Guided Skill Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
result.summary: Textual skills enable large language model (LLM) based agents to accumulate reusable procedural knowledge without updating model parameters. Yet existing skill evolution remains largely confined to the text space: an optimizer must diagnose success and failure patterns, and revise skills solely from long execution trajectories and sparse task outcomes. This text-only paradigm leaves the agent's internal representations, which contain rich records of its evolving execution state, outside the skill optimization loop. We ask whether an agent can improve its external textual skills by reflecting on its own internal representations. We introduce Rep2Skill, a representation-guided framework for self-evolution on agent skills. Specifically, upon the collected agent rollouts, Rep2Skill models their internal model representation trajectories to localize turns that deviate from successful execution dynamics, and it further interprets these signals alongside the execution contexts as actionable textual feedback for targeted skill revision. Experiments on two agent environments with two open-source LLMs show that Rep2Skill consistently outperforms text-only approaches in the self-evolution setting, where the same LLM serves as both executor and optimizer without a stronger external model. This establishes a promising direction moving agent self-improvement beyond text-only reflection.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Rep2Skill 框架，用智能体自身内部表示轨迹定位偏离成功执行动态的轮次，再把该信号与执行上下文一起转为文本反馈，用于修订文本技能，在纯文本自进化基线上取得更好效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用内部隐状态轨迹定位执行偏差的思路，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态是否承载关键信息、以及从表示中提取可用反馈/监督线索的问题相通，但场景是文本技能优化而非多模态推理，可供核查迁移。
